_about: Every requirement in the ELITE Spaces PRD v1 (Oct 6, 2026). CI/SC/EN/MB/AN/DN/AT IDs are the PRD's own. AC (users and roles) and NF (platform and non-functional) IDs are derived from those PRD sections because the PRD did not number them. gate 'test' = coverage.js requires, for EACH listed module, at least one test tagged with the ID in tests/<module>.test.js AND at least one mutation covering it in tests/mutations/<module>.js. gate 'critic' = judged by the integration critic in the browser, not automatable. gate 'retired' = a requirement retired in v1.1 (docs/v1.1-design.md); it keeps its ID and coverage.js skips it. v1.1 (Oct 28, 2026, from Stephen's answers S-1..S-15) changed some entries and added SC-5, EN-8, AN-7, DG-1..DG-3, AT-5 and MIG-1 (MIG-1 was retired the same day: no real families on v1, so v1 databases are reseeded, not migrated); the module 'integration' means tests/integration.test.js and tests/mutations/integration.js.

requirements.text: A parent creates the family account and invites each student by email or phone.
One parent account can hold several students. A student can have more than one linked parent (for example, two guardians), and each sees the same records.
Students are minors: a parent creates the account and approves the student link before the student can use the app.
Branch directors manage staff accounts for their location.
HQ admins create locations and assign directors.
Each role inherits the one below it within its scope (director > staff); HQ sees the whole network.
Each location displays a QR code at its entrance. The code rotates daily at a set time, and yesterday's code stops working.
Students check in by opening the app and scanning the code. A scan of today's code at the student's home location counts as being there: the app does not check or ask for the phone's location (S-5).

Check-in links the visit to the student's schedule for that date, including added and moved dates and excluding skipped ones. A student with no scheduled date at that time gets a clear message and cannot check in (staff can override; see CI-7).
Students check out by scanning the same code.

If a student hasn't checked out by the end of their enrolled session or the location's closing time, whichever comes first, the system checks them out automatically and flags the visit for staff review.
Parents get a push notification at each check-in and check-out, including auto-checkouts (labeled as such).
Staff can view a live 'in the building' list and manually check a student in or out (for example, a dead phone). Manual entries are logged with the staff member's name.
Directors publish schedules: a name, fixed days and one 2-3 hour time (for example, Mornings MWF 9:00-12:00), for a period with its own start and end date (a month or a semester).
Each schedule has a capacity in seats per date, based on the facility's total study space. Inside the building, students choose their own spot; the app does not assign seats.

Directors set periods (start and end dates, a month or a semester) and holiday closures. Periods at one location don't overlap. A closure cancels that date for every schedule at the location and notifies enrolled families.
Directors can edit or cancel a schedule; enrolled families are notified automatically. Once families are enrolled or waiting, its days are fixed; name, times and seats can still change.

Directors can skip, add or move a single date of one schedule (for example, Monday Nov 23 moves to Tuesday Nov 24 for a holiday). Families enrolled in it are notified, and check-in, the schedule and attendance follow the changed dates.
Enrollment is by fixed schedule: a family enrolls a student in one published schedule for its whole period and the student attends every listed date. Students do not pick individual days or weeks.
Parents enroll their students directly. Only a linked parent can enroll, join a waitlist, switch or drop.
Retired in v1.1 (S-3, D-48): students no longer request sessions; a parent picks the schedule.

Enrollment is blocked if the membership is inactive, or isn't valid on the schedule's first meeting date on or after today (not started yet, or ended before it), or if the schedule meets more days a week than the membership's weekly cap (hard cap). A membership that starts before that first date can enroll ahead of time.
When a schedule is full, families can join its waitlist. When a seat opens, the first eligible student on the list is enrolled automatically and the family is notified.
Parents can drop a schedule at any time, freeing the seat for the waitlist.
No cancellation cutoffs or no-show penalties. A missed scheduled date is simply recorded as absent; closure, skipped and moved-away dates are not.

A student holds one schedule per period. Enrolling in (or being promoted into) a schedule whose period overlaps the one held switches: the old enrollment ends, its seat goes to its waitlist, and the family gets one notice.
Each student has a membership record: status (active / inactive), weekly cap in days per week (for example, 3 or 4), start date, and expiration date.
Location staff enter and update membership records manually. The app holds no payment data.
Parents and students can see the membership status, cap and expiration date.
Parents get a reminder before the membership expires (14 and 3 days before).
On expiration or deactivation, held schedules are paused, not deleted, so they can be restored if the membership is renewed (if the seat is still free and the schedule's days fit the cap).
Directors post announcements to their location: events, workshops, holidays, session offerings and general news.
HQ admins post network-wide announcements to all locations or a chosen set.
Announcements go out as push notifications and stay in an in-app feed. Posts can be scheduled ahead of time.
Audience targeting: all families, parents only, students only, or families enrolled in a specific schedule.
Emergency alerts are a separate, high-priority type: visually distinct, cannot be muted, and go to everyone at the affected location(s). Directors (own location) and HQ (any) can send them.
Senders can see delivery and read counts.
Directors (own location) and HQ can end an emergency alert early. It stops being pinned, everyone who can see it sees it marked Ended, and its recipients get one notice that it has ended (S-11).
Staff complete a short daily note for each student who attended that day.

The note has a quick rating checklist with the same items at every location: On time, Focused, Respectful of others / not distracting, Productive use of time. Each is rated on a simple 3-point scale. HQ can edit the checklist items. The note shows the student's goals for that day beside the ratings (S-8).
The note has an optional freeform comment, which is also where staff respond to the day's goals.
Staff can complete notes quickly from the day's attendance list, with ratings defaulting to blank until set.
Parents get a notification when a note is posted and can browse past notes by date, with that day's goals in each note. Students do not see notes in v1.

After checking in, a student can set up to 3 goals for the day, each a subject (Math, English, Science, History, Language, Art, Test prep, Other, with example goals) and a sentence or two, and edit them that day. Goals need a check-in that day at the student's home location.

Setting goals is optional: the student can skip a day. Staff see, per student and day, whether goals were set, skipped or not answered. Only the student sets goals; parents see them only in posted notes.
Every check-in asks the student for today's goals (set or skip) until the day is answered, and the student Home card offers the same while it is not.
Every visit records check-in time, check-out time, total time, the session, and how check-out happened (scan, auto, staff).
Parents can view attendance history by week, month or term.
Parents can export an attendance and hours log for a chosen date range as PDF or CSV, suitable for homeschool record-keeping.
Directors and HQ can view and export attendance reports by location, schedule and date range.
When a student's scheduled day passes with no check-in at all (not a closure or skipped date, membership valid, schedule not paused), each active parent gets one notification for that day (S-12).

requirements.note: Retired Oct 28, 2026 by Justin: no real families on v1; v1 demo databases are reseeded (docs/deploy.md), so nothing migrates v1 rows and the design's flow 6 is not built.
requirements.text: On every start, the app moves v1 per-day enrollments and waiting spots to whole-schedule ones, once (idempotent). No student loses a seat to capacity (seats grow) or to the weekly cap (kept paused), no live waiting spot can later switch a student out of the schedule kept, and families and directors are told what changed.
Families see only their own data. Staff see only their location's families. HQ sees all. Every module's endpoints enforce this.
All staff edits (manual check-ins, membership changes) are logged.
Waitlist promotion runs reliably, with no double-booking when two families take the last seat at once.
Each location runs on its own time zone for sessions, closing times and QR rotation.
The app never asks for, reads or stores the phone's location. Coordinates sent with a scan are ignored, and locations need no coordinates or radius.
A check-in scan completes in under 2 seconds.
Meets WCAG 2.1 AA for contrast, text size and screen-reader labels.

Mobile-first installable web app for students and parents (QR scanning through the camera, notifications, no location permission); the same app laid out for desktop for staff, directors and HQ. iOS onboarding walks families through Add to Home Screen.
v1 succeeds if pilot locations can run day-to-day operations entirely in the app, with no paper sign-ins or spreadsheet schedules.
